name: Electric foot file

lead: An electric foot file is a handheld, battery or mains powered device with a rotating abrasive roller or disc, used to remove calluses and rough skin from the heels and soles. It automates the work of a pumice stone or manual rasp and is typically used on dry skin.

In appearance care it is used to keep heels smooth. No clinical trials of these specific devices were found; the rating rests on the long-standing practice of mechanical callus removal, and the visible effect is temporary because the skin thickens again under pressure.

paras: The abrasive head spins and shaves down the thickened stratum corneum of a callus. Because the layer is dead keratin, removal is reported to be painless when done lightly, and the skin looks and feels smoother until friction rebuilds it.

Over-use can remove too much skin, causing soreness, fissures or a rebound thicker callus, and cutting too deep risks infection. People with diabetes, neuropathy or poor circulation are generally advised to avoid home callus removal and use professional care. Podiatry guidance favors combining light filing with moisturizers such as urea creams, and avoiding blades. Heads must be cleaned or replaced between users.
